Subject: Re: sudden latency/5xx — region us-west-2

Folks —

We're seeing a sustained latency spike and ~6–8% 5xx rate hitting our inference calls to model-redwood-prod in us-west-2 starting ~16:40 PDT. Tail latency jumps (p95->p99) and client-side retransmits correlate with a large number of SYN retransmits in our edge traces. We pulled a sample of 500s (attached).

Initial notes from our SRE:
- Requests routed via VPC-peering (Redwood VPC -> EdgeMart transit) recently started crossing AZ boundaries more often (cross-AZ hairpin).
- NAT gateway translation counts increased on our side; we also see connection resets at the proxy hop.

Can you confirm whether any routing or firewall policy changes were applied on Redwood's side around 16:30-17:00? This is a production-impacting issue for our checkout path — execs are asking for updates.

Thanks,
Liam
EdgeMart — Sr. Platform Engineer

Subject: Re: sudden latency/5xx — us-west-2 traceroute + early findings

Quick update from my end — attached traceroute and packet sample included. Key findings so far:

- Traceroutes from EdgeMart's egress to our inference fleet show asymmetric pathing: some flows are routed directly to the us-west-2 AZ-a routers, while others are being steered across AZ-a -> transit -> AZ-c -> back to AZ-a. TTL and hop timing indicate an extra 2–3 hops for the slow flows. (see network-traceroute-20290504.txt)
- The extra path correlates with NAT translations on our transit gateway at the time window (16:28–16:50). We observed an ephemeral NAT mapping saturation event leading to connection resets for a subset of TCP flows.
- Firewall/proxy layer (edge proxy cluster r-proxy-12) shows increased connection queueing and a burst of 502/504 responses when the NAT mapping churn peaked. No config change was rolled by our infra team during that minute — however, an autoscaling event for the transit gateway coincided with the spike (autoscaler added 2 transit instances).

Hypothesis: a combination of transit autoscale + asymmetric route steering created transient NAT mapping churn and proxy queue pressure. That produced a class of flows with elevated RTT and connection failures.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Pin routing for EdgeMart's peering prefixes to avoid cross-AZ steering (low risk, quick).
2) Increase NAT table capacity and temporarily enable sticky mappings for prefixes with high connection rates (moderate risk).
3) Move EdgeMart traffic to an alternate AZ-local path via our direct-attach route (requires a short maintenance window).

I'm executing traceroutes across the fleet and will post more packet captures. Marcus — can you confirm whether we can pin routing for just the EdgeMart prefixes now?

— Rafael
Net Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

Also loop in Support for a customer-facing post-mortem once stabilized. Liam — will your team accept a short temporary maintenance that pins routing and may cause a ~15s connection drains for in-flight requests?

Date: Mon, 6 May 2029 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: EdgeMart incident — exec summary and next steps

Executives / Stakeholders —

Summary: On 2029-05-04 (16:28–16:52 PDT) EdgeMart experienced elevated latency and an increased rate of 5xx responses for traffic routed to our model-redwood-prod endpoint in us-west-2. Root cause analysis indicates an interaction between transit autoscaling and our NAT/transit route-steering that produced asymmetric cross-AZ paths and transient NAT mapping churn, which in turn overloaded the proxy connection queues and generated 502/504s for a subset of flows.

Immediate mitigations completed:
- Pinned EdgeMart peering prefixes to AZ-local routing (applied staged by AZ) to remove the cross-AZ hairpin (change completed at 2029-05-04T19:03:00-07:00).
- Temporarily increased NAT table capacity and enabled sticky mappings for high-connection prefixes (rolled back to autoscaling policy changes on 2029-05-05 after verification).
- Scaled proxy cluster r-proxy-12 by +2 instances to drain existing queues.

Customer impact: ~12 minutes of elevated p99 latency and a ~6–8% 5xx rate for a subset of checkout flows. EdgeMart estimates ~0.04% of purchases were affected (see HubSpot-Deal-13579 notes).

Next steps / action items:
1) Net infra to harden transit autoscaler to avoid simultaneous instance churn during burst windows (Rafael) — ETA 2 weeks.
2) Add synthetic monitoring and a targeted canary for cross-AZ steering to detect route asymmetry (Marcus) — ETA 1 week.
3) Update the VPC peering runbook with explicit NAT-table capacity checks and sticky-mapping guidance (Naomi) — ETA 3 business days.
4) Customer-facing post-mortem draft to be reviewed by Support and Legal (Vanessa) — ETA 48 hours.

I will schedule a 30-minute briefing with EdgeMart execs if they request one; otherwise, we'll proceed with the above actions and share the post-mortem. Thank you to the on-call and ops teams for the quick mitigation.

— Soojin
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
